## Next.js Development Standards

### App Router & File-Based Routing
- Use the **App Router** (`app/` directory) exclusively — the Pages Router is legacy and should not be used for new projects.
- Define layouts in `layout.tsx` files to share UI across route segments — use the root layout for global elements (header, footer, providers).
- Use **route groups** `(groupName)/` to organize routes without affecting the URL structure — separate `(auth)/` and `(dashboard)/` for distinct layout boundaries.
- Colocate page-specific components and utilities inside their route folder — **NEVER** scatter page-specific logic across global directories.
- Use `loading.tsx` for route-level Suspense fallbacks and `error.tsx` for route-level error boundaries.

### Server Components & Data Fetching
- All components in the `app/` directory are Server Components by default — only add `"use client"` when the component requires interactivity, local state, or browser APIs.
- Fetch data directly inside Server Components using `async`/`await` — colocate the fetch with the component that renders the data.
- Use `Promise.all()` for parallel independent data requests — **NEVER** create sequential waterfall fetches.
- Use React `cache()` to deduplicate identical data requests within a single render lifecycle.
- Leverage **Streaming** with `Suspense` to send parts of the page to the browser as they become ready — this dramatically improves Time to First Byte (TTFB).

### Server Actions & Mutations
- Use Server Actions (marked with `"use server"`) for all data mutations — form submissions, database writes, cache invalidation.
- **MUST** validate all inputs on the server within the action — **NEVER** trust data sent from the client.
- Keep Server Actions pure and predictable — treat them like API endpoints with no client-side state dependencies.
- Use `revalidatePath()` or `revalidateTag()` after mutations to refresh cached data — **NEVER** rely on manual client-side cache invalidation.
- **NEVER** use Server Actions for read-only data fetching — use standard Server Component data fetching for reads.

### Middleware & Security
- Use `middleware.ts` as a global interception layer for authentication, redirects, and request headers.
- **NEVER** rely solely on middleware for authorization — always perform a second identity check inside Server Actions and API Route handlers (defense in depth).
- Use `httpOnly` and `secure` cookies for session management — **NEVER** store authentication tokens in `localStorage` or client-accessible cookies.
- Sanitize all user inputs at the Server Action boundary to prevent injection attacks.

### Performance & Caching
- Use static rendering (`generateStaticParams`) for pages with known, finite datasets — product pages, blog posts, documentation.
- Use ISR (`revalidate` option) for content that changes periodically but does not require real-time freshness.
- Use dynamic rendering only for personalized or real-time content — **NEVER** make every page dynamic by default.
- Optimize images with the `next/image` component — it handles lazy loading, responsive sizing, and format conversion automatically.
- Use `next/font` for font loading — it eliminates layout shift by self-hosting fonts with zero external requests.

### Project Structure
- Place all source code inside `src/` to keep the project root clean.
- `src/app/`: Routing, layouts, and page-level Server Components.
- `src/components/`: Shared UI components organized by feature or domain.
- `src/lib/`: Server-side utilities, database clients, and configuration.
- `src/hooks/`: Client-side custom hooks.
- `src/actions/`: Server Actions organized by domain (e.g., `auth.ts`, `cart.ts`).
